story.titleZh: 维斯塔潘与红牛新约：赢家与输家
story.summaryZh: 在超过一年的续约悬念之后，马克斯·维斯塔潘与红牛签下一份重磅新合同，尽管表面维持现状，却立即重塑了F1车手市场的格局。The 比赛分析了这一消息的赢家与输家。

story.originalTitle: Winners and losers from Verstappen's big new Red Bull F1 deal
story.summaryEn: After more than a year of intrigue about his future, Max Verstappen has signed a major new contract with Red Bull, which instantly reshapes the F1 driver market despite seemingly maintaining the status quo. The Race looks at the winners and losers from the news.
detailZh: 在经过一年多关于维斯塔潘未来的猜疑之后，Verstappen与红牛之间的一份新合同，立即重塑了F1车手市场的格局——尽管表面上似乎维持了现状。
以下是我们对这一重大新闻中谁是赢家、谁是输家的看法。
显然，具体的财务条款不会公开，但我们可以放心地假设，这将是红牛付出一个小型大洋洲国家全年GDP的成本——并且大概还会附加一些额外许可，让Verstappen可以参与F1之外的赛车活动。
但是……随它去吧！红牛一下子从一个步履蹒跚的F1巨头，变成了一个不再需要担心失去其最大资产的、步履蹒跚的F1巨头——而这份资产同时也是整个围场上任何F1车队所拥有的最了不起的资产。
如果2027年的赛车特别糟糕，谣言在某种程度上会重新燃起，但这对红牛来说是一次巨大的胜利——并再次确认了它在未来数年内作为F1顶级车队之一的地位。
输家：卡洛斯·塞恩斯、奥斯卡·皮亚斯特里以及其他'梦想家'
塞恩斯与威廉姆斯的新合同——现在真的感觉像是'不妨就这样吧'——在维斯塔潘续约的前一天宣布，这恐怕并非巧合。
塞恩斯会是取代维斯塔潘在红牛位置的主要候选人吗？很可能不是。但车手市场的任何变动都会有利于他重返积分榜上半区的机会——而维斯塔潘决定离开F1（现在已确定没有发生），本会在'四大豪门'中制造一个小小的车手空缺，而塞恩斯本会是填补这一空缺的头号（或接近头号）人选。
维斯塔潘留队，切断了所有“梦想家”们的各种选择。这不仅仅是指中游车队的车手——如果像皮亚斯特里这样的人在迈凯伦真的感到不安，并且对领导红牛这样一支车队的前景有丝毫心动的话，这条路现在已经被长期封死了。而任何一直觊觎红牛的人现在都会明白，转会到那里将意味着，正如长期以来一直如此的那样，要正面迎战F1中最令人生畏的车手。
对于梅基斯在红牛至今为止的第一年多的时间，可以从几个角度来看待。2025年底的成绩很强，2026年迄今也不算糟糕，但正如我的同事艾德·斯特劳在最近的一篇专栏中相当有说服力地指出的那样，梅基斯时代的红牛似乎面临着失去其曾经独特之处的风险。
但梅基斯时代的红牛留住了维斯塔潘。尽管人才流失严重——如今已扩展到即将转会迈凯伦的比赛工程师吉安皮耶罗·兰比亚塞，以及据报道将加盟凯迪拉克的总工程师保罗·莫纳汉——洛朗·梅基斯还是留住了马克斯·维斯塔潘。
而且有很多理由怀疑，在克里斯蒂安·霍纳领导下的红牛，这次续约是否会发生。
对于阿斯顿·马丁（阿斯顿·马丁）来说，2026年有比追求大手笔签下车手这种不切实际的想法更重要的事情要做。
但现在，即使AMR底盘在阿德里安·纽维的带领下取得巨大进步，本田引擎也赶上来达到体面水平，阿斯顿·马丁也没有轻松的按钮可按来组建一个精英车手阵容。
你当然可以怀疑它是否曾经有能力吸引维斯塔潘。我自己也不太相信。但它或许本可以利用维斯塔潘的转会来为自己谋利，从而签下因此被挤走的任何车手。
但现在F1中所有最好的车手其实都没有需要做出的决定，而一旦费尔南多·阿隆索退役，阿斯顿·马丁可能不得不最大限度地利用中游方案来解决其车手问题。
当然，这是假设这辆车能真正具备竞争力。
维斯塔潘（Verstappen）逼近、可能前来夺走乔治·拉塞尔（拉塞尔）梅赛德斯席位的阴影——那本该是他的席位，基米·安东内利（安东内利）2026年的开局已经三重确保了这一点——如今已不复存在。
尽管拉塞尔本赛季至今的表现起伏不定，但从中期来看，梅赛德斯仍是他应该待的地方。如果他想成为世界冠军——他当然想——那么从安东内利手中夺回主导权，并寄希望于梅赛德斯的竞争力能够保持，是他实现这一目标的绝对最佳且“最轻松”的路径。
这在2026年可能不会实现，但可能在2027年实现，而且他已经不再承受来自唯一一位梅赛德斯可能追求作为立即升级人选的车手的外部压力。
第一——像现任车手伊斯克·哈贾尔、阿尔维德·林德布拉德，或许还有利亚姆·劳森，以及很可能是F2的尼古拉·措洛夫这样的车手，现在可供争取的红牛车队席位少了一个，整个车手阵容中的空缺位置也少了一个。
诚然，如果维斯塔潘离开，红牛肯定会从外部引进车手——但无论如何情况就是如此。
第二——所有这些车手，如果他们如愿取得进步，迟早都要与维斯塔潘正面对抗，而正如我们所知，这很可能是让你的F1生涯脱轨甚至毁掉的好办法。
维斯塔潘与红牛的新约必须被看作是对F1目前正在推行的这套他深恶痛绝的规则体系的一次信任投票。
整个赛季以来，他对这种F1赛车规则多少流露出一些厌倦，而考虑到他态度之强烈，维斯塔潘能忍受整个规则周期原本看起来确实不太可能。
现在他留下了。虽然我们肯定还会不时听到维斯塔潘对当前规则状态的批评，但最强车手因为不尊重这项产品而拂袖而去——这种最大的尴尬总算得以避免。
还记得F1车手过去常常换车队吗？那真是美好。
刘易斯·汉密尔顿转投法拉利是一记震撼，但在F1的整体趋势中似乎只是个异数——如今无论是顶尖车手还是越来越多的中游车手，都倾向于长期合同带来的财务保障，而车队也有能力提供这种保障。
这种感觉在车队积分榜顶端尤为明显。除了法拉利——汉密尔顿的年龄是一个问号——以及红牛车队那个不断换人的二号车手席位之外，各大强队的车手阵容在中期内似乎都被'冻结'了。
当前合同激励条款的现实情况——以及车手适应新车队的困难——似乎造就了一个更接近于棒球界给超级巨星开出的15年长约的市场，而不是我们更熟悉的F1那种抢座位游戏。
detailEn: A new deal between Max Verstappen and Red Bull, coming after well over a year of intrigue about Verstappen's future, has immediately reshaped the landscape of Formula 1's driver market - despite seemingly maintaining the status quo.
Here is our view of who the winners and losers are from this major piece of news.

Obviously no financial terms will be disclosed, but we can safely make the assumption that this will cost Red Bull the full GDP of a small Oceanian nation - and will presumably come with extra allowances for Verstappen in terms of exploring non-F1 racing activities.

But...like, whatever! In one fell swoop Red Bull has gone from a limping F1 giant to a limping F1 giant that doesn't have to worry about losing its greatest asset - who doubles as probably the greatest asset any F1 team up and down the grid has.
Rumours will re-fire in some capacity if the 2027 car is particularly bad, but this is a huge victory for Red Bull - and a reaffirmation of its status as one of F1's top dogs for years to come.
Losers: Carlos Sainz, Oscar Piastri and other 'dreamers'
It's probably no coincidence that Sainz's new Williams deal - which now really feels like a 'might as well' - was announced the day before a Verstappen extension.

Would Sainz have been a lead candidate to replace Verstappen at Red Bull? Likely not. But any driver market movement will have been good for his chances to returning to the top half of the grid - and Verstappen deciding to step away from F1, which now has conclusively not happened, will have created a small driver vacuum among the 'big four' that Sainz would've been top-of-the-queue (or close to it) to fill.

Verstappen staying cuts off options for all the 'dreamers'. And this doesn't have to just mean the midfield drivers - if someone like, say, Piastri is truly unsettled at McLaren and was at all tempted by the prospect of leading a team like Red Bull instead, that avenue is now shut off for a long time. And anyone who had been eyeing Red Bull will now know that a move there will mean, as it has for a long time, going up against the most fearsome driver in F1.

There are a few ways you could view the first year and a bit of Mekies at Red Bull up to now. Results were strong in late 2025 and not exactly terrible in 2026 so far, but as my colleague Edd Straw argued quite convincingly in a recent column, the Mekies-era Red Bull seemed at risk of losing what had made it special before.

But the Mekies-era Red Bull has kept Verstappen. Despite the brain drain, which has now extended to McLaren-bound race engineer Gianpiero Lambiase and reportedly Cadillac-bound chief engineer Paul Monaghan, Laurent Mekies has kept Max Verstappen.
And there's a lot of reason to doubt this extension would have happened at Christian Horner's Red Bull.
Aston Martin has much bigger fish to fry in 2026 than fanciful pursuits of big-money driver signings.

But now even if the AMR chassis makes huge strides under Adrian Newey and the Honda engine catches up to respectability, Aston Martin has no easy button to press for assembling an elite driver line-up.

You can certainly doubt whether it would have ever been able to attract Verstappen. I am not sure I believe it myself. But it may have been able to use a Verstappen move to its advantage, to secure whoever is displaced.
But now all the best drivers in F1 don't really have decisions to make, and once Fernando Alonso retires Aston Martin may have to make the most of midfield solutions to its driver question.
That is, of course, assuming the car becomes truly competitive.
The looming spectre of Verstappen coming to take George Russell’s Mercedes seat - and it would be his seat, Kimi Antonelli's start to 2026 has made triple-sure of that - is gone.

As shaky as Russell's year has been so far, Mercedes is the right place for him to be in the medium term. If he wants to be champion, and of course he does, then wrestling control back from Antonelli and hoping that Mercedes' competitive level keeps up is his absolute best and 'easiest' path to doing so.

It probably won't happen in '26, but it could happen in '27, and he's no longer under any outside pressure from the only driver that it would make sense for Mercedes to pursue as an immediate upgrade.

One - drivers like incumbent Isack Hadjar, Arvid Lindblad, maybe Liam Lawson and probably Formula 2's Nikola Tsolov now have one fewer Red Bull Racing seat to target and one fewer free spot in the overall roster.
Admittedly, had Verstappen left Red Bull would have surely pursued an outside recruit - but nonetheless.
Two - all of those drivers, if they progress as they hope, will have to go up against Verstappen at some point, which as we know is a great way to derail or potentially ruin your F1 career.
Verstappen's new Red Bull commitment must be taken as a vote of confidence in the steps F1 is taking with the current ruleset that he hates.

He has sounded some degree of fed up with this kind of F1 racing all through the season, and Verstappen putting up with the full regulations cycle genuinely felt unlikely given the strength of feeling on his end.

Now he stays. And while we will surely hear more criticism here and there from Verstappen as to the state of the formula, the ultimate embarrassment of having your strongest driver walk away because he doesn't respect the product is averted.
Remember when F1 drivers used to, like, change teams? That was nice.

Lewis Hamilton's switch to Ferrari was a jolt but seemed an aberration in the general trend of F1 - which is drivers, both top and increasingly midfield, favouring the financial security of long-term commitments and teams having the means to provide that security.

It is particularly felt at the top of the grid. Apart from Ferrari, where Hamilton's age is a question mark, and that revolving-door second Red Bull seat, the top teams appear 'frozen' for the medium term.

The current realities of contractual incentives - and the difficulty in adapting to new teams - seem to have created a market that's closer to the 15-year deals they hand out to superstars in baseball than the game of musical chairs that we're more used to in F1.
keyPointsZh: 维斯塔潘的未来悬念已持续超过一年
合同财务条款不会公开，外界推测金额巨大，并可能允许维斯塔潘参与F1以外的赛车活动
红牛虽然保住了队内最大资产，但仍面临车队表现方面的挑战
keyPointsEn: The intrigue over Verstappen's future had lasted well over a year
Financial terms will not be disclosed, but the deal is assumed to be hugely expensive and may include allowances for Verstappen to explore non-F1 racing activities
Red Bull retains its greatest asset but remains a struggling F1 giant

relatedItems.originalTitle: Jos Verstappen was hyped like Max - until it all went wrong
relatedItems.summaryEn: The article recalls how Jos Verstappen impressed in a Footwork test at Estoril in 1993, generating huge excitement and landing on the cover of Autosport magazine as 'F1's hottest new boy'.
detailZh: 乔斯·维斯塔潘自己在F1的失意，在多大程度上推动了他为儿子马克斯备战后来堪称现象级的F1生涯倾注一切，这已是赛车运动中的民间传说。
如今或许被忽视的一点是，乔斯自己的F1生涯本应有多出色——曾经有那么一段时间（诚然很短暂），人们对乔斯成为未来F1冠军的期待，与2015年马克斯进入F1发车格时一样热烈。
正如我们与埃德·斯特劳和马克·休斯合作的新一季F1 Rewind播客系列最新一集所探讨的，真正开启这波热潮的，是1993年9月底在埃斯托里尔为Footwork车队进行的一次测试。
当时乔斯离开卡丁车仅两年，刚刚赢得德国F3锦标赛冠军，21岁的他做出的圈速，若放在前一周葡萄牙大奖赛排位赛中，足以让他那辆非常平庸的赛车排在第10位。赛道状况的演变对他的圈速有所影响，但他的整体表现给人留下了巨大印象。维斯塔潘登上了下一周《Autosport》杂志的封面，该杂志称他为“F1最炙手可热的新人”。
埃德·斯特劳：“如果你看看乔斯·维斯塔潘的职业生涯记录，却没有亲身经历过，就很容易低估这次测试产生的巨大影响。”
马克·休斯：“他当时是备受追捧的抢手人物。他从卡丁车直接进入贝内卢克斯锦标赛的GM Lotus车队，并立即赢得冠军。他曾在斯帕赛道更高级别的GM Lotus系列赛中做过一次客串出场。那场比赛他表现惊艳。
“他直接升入三级方程式，赢得德国锦标赛，统治了赛场，看起来注定要在F1赛道上大放异彩。
“各支车队争相抢着要给他一份长期合同。如果你在寻找下一个迈克尔·舒马赫或米卡·哈基宁可能在哪里，那就是你要找的地方。毫无疑问。”
埃德·斯特劳：“基本上所有人都在和他谈。迈凯伦曾在某个阶段给他安排了一次测试。显然还有贝纳通，他最终签约的车队。甚至法拉利也有一点兴趣。那绝对是一场哄抢，因为这就是下一个超级巨星。
“也因为他的上升速度太快了。两年内从卡丁车到F1。近年来我们已经有点习惯非常快的晋升了，比如马克斯·维斯塔潘。但在那个时候，这真的非常非常罕见。
“所以你不仅拥有这位被认为不可思议的车手，而且他还坐着这艘火箭飞船直奔F1。
“如果在1993年底你问，‘好，谁将进入F1赢得比赛并成为未来的世界冠军？’约斯·维斯塔潘就是人们会挑出的名字。”
马克·休斯：“在那个时候绝对是压倒性的。毫无疑问。他正处于重大突破的边缘。”
维斯塔潘和经纪人胡布·罗滕加特选择了贝纳通车队，该车队提供1994年一个赛季的测试和准备工作，然后保证1995年的正式比赛席位——要么在自家车队，要么安排到其他地方。
但维斯塔潘并没有在聚光灯外获得一年的学习时间，而是当JJ·莱赫托在测试撞车中受伤后，他被推上了贝纳通的第二个比赛席位，与迈克尔·舒马赫并肩作战。
维斯塔潘最终在那个席位上两度登场，因为莱赫托回归后仍然挣扎，不得不再次退出，之后他在赛季末被按在替补席上，以便贝纳通评估约翰尼·赫伯特在那辆车上的表现。
这加起来是1994赛季16站中的10站，他驾驶第二辆贝纳通车队赛车，维斯塔潘两次登上领奖台，但也在巴西站首秀中被埃迪·欧文引发的一起连环事故送入一次令人恐惧的腾空撞车，还卷入了臭名昭著的德国大奖赛维修区火灾。
后来他承认，那辆以舒马赫为中心的赛车对他来说“过于敏感”，在他们共同出战的八场比赛中，维斯塔潘从未在排位赛中击败舒马赫，甚至从未在比赛圈结束时领先过舒马赫，平均差距高达1.920秒（2.288%）。
作为准备不足的新秀，在同一车队中与舒马赫对抗，又处在一个动荡的赛季中，这是一项艰巨的任务。而这足以瞬间粉碎维斯塔潘带入F1的所有职业势头和炒作。
马克·休斯：“事后看来，他还没准备好，他来得太早了。如果最初的计划得以实施，他本会在远离大奖赛聚光灯的地方积累大量里程，并且可能在1995年准备得充分得多地到来。
“不仅如此，贝纳通车队完全是以迈克尔·舒马赫为中心，而车队老板弗拉维奥·布里亚托雷则涉足车手管理，然后靠车手赚钱。
“罗滕加特和维斯塔潘在不知不觉中交出了对自己命运的控制权。维斯塔潘不仅在一支完全围绕一名车手打造的车队里开着实质上只是第二梯队的赛车，他甚至都无法掌控自己下一步要去哪里。”
埃德·斯特劳：“他经历了这样一个奇怪的赛季，实际上那第一赛季就抹掉了他职业生涯势头的很大一部分。确实如此，真的真的如此。势头并没有完全消失，还残留着一点‘哦这家伙不错’的印象，但基本上大局已定。”
马克·休斯：“当你陷入那种境地——你是二号车手，不是任何事情的焦点——这会消耗你的精力。而你此前一直习惯于处在一切事物的绝对中心，习惯于被当作一颗正在冉冉升起的巨星来对待，在青训车队里一切都围绕着你，所有人都为你而来，所有人都站在你这边。突然之间沦为一个跟班的角色，我认为这确实会对你造成伤害。
“不仅如此，你还要作为一名新秀去对抗迈克尔·舒马赫。
“而在后来更能反思的岁月里，维斯塔潘也说，即使不考虑装备差异——贝纳通当时确实存在显著的装备差异——即使不考虑所有对他不利的因素，当你近距离看到迈克尔能够做到的一些事情时，你突然不得不对自己说：‘我进来时以为我会赢比赛，我以为我会赢冠军，我会打败所有人’，然后你遇到那样一个人，你会想：‘不，也许我得在这里重新校准。’
“甚至维斯塔潘也承认，也许他并不是迈克尔·舒马赫。
“但他相当出色。比他后来能够展现出来的还要好。”
观看或收听《F1 Rewind》节目，了解更多关于乔斯（Jos）的F1职业生涯，包括后来错失的重大机会，并深入探讨这一切如何影响了他对马克斯（Max）的养育方式以及马克斯通往F1的旅程。
detailEn: The degree to which Jos Verstappen’s own Formula 1 disappointment fuelled everything he poured into son Max’s preparation for his ultimately-phenomenal F1 career is already part of motorsport folklore.

The element that perhaps gets overlooked now is how good Jos’s own F1 career was supposed to be - that there was a period, a short one admittedly, when there was just as much excitement over Jos’s prospects as a future F1 champion as there was over Max’s arrival on the F1 grid in 2015.
As the latest episode of our new F1 Rewind podcast series with Edd Straw and Mark Hughes explores, it’s a test for Footwork at Estoril in late September 1993 that really starts the hype.

Only two years out of karting, and having just won the German Formula 3 title, 21-year-old Jos sets a time that would’ve put his very middling car 10th on the grid for the previous weekend’s Portuguese Grand Prix. Track evolution played a part in his time, but the impression his overall performance makes is huge. Verstappen gets the cover slot on the next week’s Autosport magazine, which declares him ‘F1’s hottest new boy’.
Edd Straw: “If you look at Jos Verstappen's career record and didn't experience it or live through it, it's really easy to underestimate how big an impact this test really made."

Mark Hughes: “He was a seriously hot property at that time. He came straight in from karting and won championship immediately in GM Lotus in the Benelux Championship. He'd done a one-off guest appearance in the bigger league GM Lotus series at Spa. He was sensational in that.
“He moved straight to Formula 3, won the German championship, dominated it, and looked set to set the F1 tracks alight.

“The teams were falling over themselves trying to get him on a long-term contract. If you were looking for where the next Michael Schumacher or Mika Hakkinen might be, that's where you are looking. No question.”

Edd Straw: “Everybody was talking to him basically. McLaren gave him a test at one stage. Obviously Benetton, who he eventually signed for. There was a little bit of Ferrari interest even. It was an absolute clamour because this was the next mega-star.

“Also because of how rapid his ascent was. Karting to F1 in two years. In recent years we’ve got a bit more used to really fast ascents, such as Max Verstappen’s. But that was really, really rare at this point.
“So you've not only got this driver who is considered to be incredible, but he's on this rocketship to F1 as well.
“And if in late 1993 you were saying, ‘right, who is going to come into F1 and win races and be a future world champion?’ Jos Verstappen is the name people would have picked out.”
Mark Hughes: “Overwhelmingly at that time. There was no question. He was on the verge of something big.”

Verstappen and manager Huub Rothengatter pick Benetton, which is offering a season of testing and preparation in 1994 then a guaranteed race seat - either in its own squad, or placed elsewhere - for 1995.
But rather than getting a year of learning outside the spotlight, Verstappen is thrust into Benetton’s second race seat alongside Michael Schumacher when JJ Lehto is injured in a testing crash.

Verstappen ultimately gets two stints in that seat, with Lehto still struggling on his return and having to step away again, before being benched at the end of the season so Benetton can evaluate Johnny Herbert in that car.

It adds up to 10 of the 16 1994 rounds in the second Benetton, with Verstappen earning two podiums, but also being sent into a terrifying aerial crash on his debut in Brazil in a pile-up triggered by Eddie Irvine and being caught up in the infamous German GP pit fire.

Later admitting he found the Schumacher-centric car “too nervous” for him, Verstappen never outqualified or even once led Schumacher at the end of a racing lap in their eight outings together with a massive 1.920s (2.288%) average deficit.

Going up against Schumacher in the same team as an underprepared rookie, amid a season of turmoil, was a tall order. And it was enough to instantly crush all that career momentum and hype Verstappen had carried into F1.

Mark Hughes: “In hindsight, he wasn't ready, he came in too early. Had the original plan played out, he would have been getting a lot of mileage away from the spotlight of grands prix and would have probably come in much better prepared in 1995.
“Not only that, Benetton was absolutely centred around Michael Schumacher and team boss Flavio Briatore was into driver management and then making money on drivers.

“Rothengatter and Verstappen had unknowingly surrendered control of his own destiny. As well as being in essentially just the second string car in a team that was totally focused around one driver, Verstappen wasn't even going to be in charge of where he was going to go next.”

Edd Straw: “He has this weird season and actually a big chunk of that career momentum's wiped out by that first season. It really, really is. It's not gone. There's still a residual, ‘oh this guy's good’, but already pretty much the die is cast.”

Mark Hughes: “It saps you of energy when you get into a situation like that where you're the second driver and you're not the focus of anything. And you've been used to being at the absolute centre of everything. You've been used to being treated as a megastar in the making and with everything centred around you in the junior category, with everybody there for you, everybody on your side. And suddenly to be in the lackey role, I think it does damage you.
“And not only that, but you're going up against Michael Schumacher as a rookie.

“And in his more reflective later years, Verstappen also said that even disregarding the equipment differences - and there were significant equipment differences at Benetton - and even disregarding all the factors against him, when you looked at some of the things that Michael was able to do close up and suddenly have to say to yourself, ‘I came in thinking I was going to win races, I think I'm going to win the championship, I'm going to beat everybody’ and then you come up against somebody like that and you think, ‘no, maybe I have to recalibrate here’.
“And even Verstappen acknowledges that maybe he wasn't Michael Schumacher.
“But he was pretty good. Better than he was able to show subsequently.”

Watch or listen to F1 Rewind for much more on Jos’s F1 career, including the later big opportunities that fell through, and an in-depth look at how it all fed into the way he handled Max’s upbringing and journey towards F1.
keyPointsZh: 1993年9月底，21岁的乔斯·维斯塔潘在埃斯托里尔为Footwork车队测试，做出的圈速若放在前一周葡萄牙大奖赛排位赛中，足以让他那辆表现平平的赛车排在第10位。
赛道状况的演变对他的圈速有所影响，但他的整体表现给人留下了深刻印象，随后登上《Autosport》杂志封面。
埃德·斯特劳指出，如果不曾亲历，很容易低估这次测试产生的巨大影响；马克·休斯则称他当时是“非常抢手的人物”。
keyPointsEn: In late September 1993, 21-year-old Jos Verstappen tested for Footwork at Estoril, setting a time that would have placed his middling car 10th on the grid for the previous weekend's Portuguese Grand Prix.
Track evolution played a part in his time, but the overall impression was huge, leading to the cover of Autosport magazine.
Edd Straw noted it is easy to underestimate the impact of this test without experiencing it, while Mark Hughes called him 'a seriously hot property' at the time.

relatedItems.originalTitle: Verstappen has troubled qualifying in latest GT outing
relatedItems.summaryEn: Max Verstappen, competing in the GT World Challenge at Portimao between Formula 1 races, will start only 15th with teammates Chris Lulham and Ben Barnicoat. After an incident in practice that drew no penalty, the team admitted they took a wrong turn with the setup.
detailZh: 马克斯·维斯塔潘与队友克里斯·卢勒姆和本·巴尼科特将在波尔蒂芒GT世界挑战赛中仅从第15位发车，维斯塔潘是在F1比赛间隙参加这场比赛。
维斯塔潘重返GT赛场开局波折，在上午练习赛的第一圈因交通拥堵追尾了埃泽奎尔·佩雷斯·孔潘克的奥迪，导致其打转。
赛会干事查看了该事件但未采取行动，到第二节练习赛结束时，维斯塔潘车组已升至第四。
但他们在排位赛中挣扎，他们的梅赛德斯赛车明显比大多数赛车更低，在暮色中擦出大量火花，最终在61辆赛车的发车格上仅列第15。
虽然巴尼科特称第15名是“本可能更糟”的情况，但他承认由2 Seas Motorsport运营的维斯塔潘车队在调校上走错了方向。
“我们感觉一直缺少一点速度——我们在成绩榜上排名相当靠前，但我们中没有一个人特别满意，”他说。
“所以我们尝试了几项调整，显然效果不太理想——大量火花、直道上很多弹跳，所以我认为我们只是稍微没找准。”
这场三小时的比赛于当地时间周六下午5点开始。Dorian Boccalacci、Morris Schuring和Alessio Picariello驾驶的Boutsen VDS保时捷从杆位起步。
detailEn: Max Verstappen and team-mate Chris Lulham and Ben Barnicoat will start only 15th for the GT World Challenge race at Portimao that Verstappen is contesting in his break between Formula 1 races.
Verstappen's return to the GT scene got off to an eventful start as he tapped Ezequiel Perez Companc's Audi into a spin in a traffic jam on his first lap in morning practice.
Stewards looked at the incident but took no action, and by the end of the second practice session the Verstappen crew was up to fourth.
But they struggled in qualifying, their Mercedes visibly running lower than most and kicking up abundant sparks in the twilight session as they managed only 15th on the 61-car grid.
While Barnicoat called 15th a "could be worse" situation, he admitted the 2 Seas Motorsport-run Verstappen team had taken a wrong turn with the set-up.
"We felt like we'd been missing a little bit of speed - we've been quite high up the timesheets but none of us were super happy," he said.
"So we tried a couple of things there and obviously it didn't quite work out - lots of sparking, a lot of bouncing in a straight line, so I think we just missed it a little bit."
The three-hour race starts at 5pm local time on Saturday. The Boutsen VDS Porsche of Dorian Boccalacci, Morris Schuring and Alessio Picariello starts from pole.

第二节练习赛结束时，维斯塔潘车组排名升至第四。
排位赛中他们的梅赛德斯赛车明显比大多数赛车更低，在暮色中擦出大量火花，最终在61辆赛车中仅列第15。

By the end of the second practice session, the Verstappen crew was up to fourth.
In qualifying, their Mercedes visibly ran lower than most and kicked up abundant sparks in the twilight session, managing only 15th on the 61-car grid.
